title: Overrides in force, from the trail alone

blocks.text: Riverbend Water's (invented for this practice) audit trail is append-only. Each entry is a dict with a sequence number `seq`, an `action`, a `project`, a `kind`, a `year` and who made it, when and why. The actions are:

items: `set`: the override becomes the one in force for its project, replacing any earlier one;
`inherit`: the same as `set`, written when a plan is copied with its overrides;
`refused`: a request that was turned down; it changes nothing;
`clear`: a manager resets the plan; every override in force ends (its `project` is empty).

blocks.text: Entries may reach you in any order, for example merged from two pages of a query.
Write `in_force(entries)` in `replay.py`. It returns `{project: (kind, year)}` for the overrides in force after every entry has been applied in the order the entries were made. About ten lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from replay import in_force


def entry(seq, action, project="", kind="", year=None):
    return {"seq": seq, "action": action, "project": project, "kind": kind, "year": year,
            "by": "planner-x", "why": "review"}


trail = [entry(4, "set", "P-5", "start_in", 2033), entry(1, "set", "P-5", "start_in", 2031),
         entry(2, "set", "P-9", "out"), entry(3, "revoke", "P-9", "out")]
print("four entries:", in_force(trail))
print("plus an inherit at seq 5:", in_force(trail + [entry(5, "inherit", "P-2", "out")]))
print("plus a clear at seq 6 and a set at seq 7:",
      in_force(trail + [entry(6, "clear"), entry(7, "set", "P-1", "start_in", 2032)]))

cases.says: two set entries on two projects are both in force
a second set on the same project replaces the first
entries listed out of order are replayed by their sequence numbers
a revoked override and a refused request leave nothing in force
a clear entry ends every override set before it, inherited ones included

origin.section: The Trail Records Who, When, Why and the Bounds That Moved, and Is Only Ever Appended To

concepts: supersedes and revocations are new entries, and the overrides in force are rebuilt by replaying them in order
